analysis: Gp2b3A inhibitors are a class of antiplatelet drugs that target the glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor on platelets, thereby inhibiting platelet aggregation. The drugs Abciximab, Eptifibatide, and Tirofiban are well-known members of this class. Prasugrel, however, is not a Gp2b3A inhibitor; it is a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor, which works through a different mechanism to prevent platelet aggregation. This distinction is well-established in pharmacology, and there is a clear consensus that Prasugrel does not belong to the Gp2b3A inhibitor class.
